newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 8.

text.p: Esso Sekiyu K.K. plans to cut its workforce by about 16 percent, or by 170 to 180 employees, by the end of December. About 150 of them have decided to join its early retirement programme, and will leave the company by the end of this year.

Kuroda Precision Industries Ltd plans to set up a joint venture in Malaysia next spring to make precision molds for motors, in cooperation with the Kawasho Corp group. The venture, to be capitalised at about 100 million yen, will be owned 70 percent by Kuroda and 30 percent by Kawasho.

Oil company Idemitsu Kosan Co Ltd confirmed further oil reserves in two North Sea fields where it owns concession rights. Output at the oil fields are estimated at between 29,600 and 34,000 barrels a day. Commercial production will start in two or three years.
Leading Internet service provider Tokyo Internet to merge with its largest sales dealer Secom Internet Service Co Ltd on December 1. The company will be capitalised at 730 million yen.
